hero.title: Write a problem. Prove it. Let anyone solve it.
hero.lead: Verdale is an online judge where the problems come from you. Publish one when your own solution passes every test, group problems into Tracks, and invite anyone to solve them.
hero.signInHint: Sign in with your GitHub or Google account.
hero.previewLabel: A Verdale solve page: C++ code in the editor and twelve tests judged one by one until the submission is Accepted.

sides.title: Built for the person who writes the problem and the person who solves it.

points.statements: Statements in Markdown with math, or a PDF up to 10 pages
points.testcases: Upload testcases and generate expected output from your own solution
points.publish: Publish only when your reference solution passes every test
points.edit: Edit after publishing: each change becomes a new version that is checked again

points.statements: Clear statements with samples you can copy in one click
points.samples: Run the samples before you submit
points.failures: See which test failed, with time and memory for each one
points.progress: Follow your progress through every Track you join

how.title: From a blank page to a judged submission in four steps.

write.title: Write it
write.text: Write the statement in Markdown with math, set time and memory limits, and add your testcases.

prove.title: Prove it
prove.text: Attach a reference solution. The problem can only be published once it passes every one of your tests.

publish.title: Publish it
publish.text: Put the problem in a Collection, add it to a Track, and invite people by name or with a link.

solve.title: Solve it
solve.text: Solvers submit code and get a verdict for every test, with the time and memory it used.

spaces.title: Run a class, a club or a camp from one Space.
spaces.lead: A Space holds your problems and your people. Tracks are the paths solvers follow, Collections are ordered sets of problems inside them, and roles with permissions decide who can see and change what.
spaces.previewLabel: Example Space Algorithms 101 with two Tracks. Week 2 Hashing holds the Collection Warm-up with three problems: one Accepted, one Wrong answer, one not tried.
spaces.note: A Collection can sit in several Tracks, and a problem in several Collections. Solvers see only the Tracks they belong to.

roles.name: Roles
roles.text: Each member of a Space has a role, from managing the whole Space to only solving problems.

permissions.name: Permissions
permissions.text: A role sets what someone can change, such as members, problems and testcases, and what they can see.

trackAccess.name: Track access
trackAccess.text: Solvers see only the Tracks they belong to, and hidden testcases stay hidden from them.

spaces.invite: Invite people one by one or with a link that expires. Revoke a link at any time.

judge.title: A judge you can trust with hidden tests.
judge.lead: Every submission and every reference solution runs in the same isolated sandbox, so a verdict means the same thing for everyone.

languages.title: Multiple languages
languages.text: Solve in the language you prefer. Every language is compiled and run by the same judge.

sandbox.title: Sandboxed runs
sandbox.text: Every run is isolated, with no network and hard limits on time, memory and processes.

hidden.title: Hidden tests stay hidden
hidden.text: Solvers see the visible samples. The other testcases never leave the server.

oneJudge.title: One judge for both sides
oneJudge.text: Your reference solution runs in the same sandbox as every submission.

results.title: Results for every test
results.text: Watch each test finish as it is judged, then see its time and memory.

limits.title: Fair use limits
limits.text: Submissions are rate limited per person, so one busy solver cannot hold up the queue.

judge.verdictsText: Every result carries its name and an icon, never colour alone.

closing.title: Start with one problem.
closing.text: Sign in, create a Space and publish when your solution passes. The people you invite can start solving right away.
closing.tagline: Write a problem. Prove it. Let anyone solve it.
